title: Geodesic timber dome
summary: chord factors, strut schedule, laser-cut hubs
description: A timber-strut geodesic dome (1V, 2V or 3V) with laser-cut steel hubs: give a radius or a floor area and get the strut schedule, the timber to buy, the hub count and the plates to send to the laser.
process: Sawn timber struts with bolted steel-in-timber connections; laser-cut, welded and galvanised steel hubs

difficulty.rationale: Frequency-dependent topology with hand-derived 3D placements and coupled limits over many bodies.

standards: Domerama, chord factor charts (1V, 2V, 3V chord factors, strut and face counts)
Desert Domes, 2V and 3V dome calculators (strut and connector counts for 2V, 3V 3/8 and 3V 5/8)
EN 1995-1-1:2004+A1:2008, table 8.4 (bolt spacing and edge and end distances) and clause 10.4.3 (hole sizes, washers)
EN 338 strength class C24, mean density 420 kg/m3 (via Taylor Maxwell strength data)
EN 10219-2 cold-formed circular hollow sections 60.3 x 4 and 76.1 x 4 mm for the hub tube
ISO 4017 bolt head height and ISO 4032 nut height (values listed by Würth and Kramp for the nuts)
BS 5268-2:2002 (withdrawn) maximum slenderness 180 for compression members (via RoyMech Timber Axial)
materials: Sawn spruce C24, 38 x 89 to 63 x 175 mm
Steel plate 3 to 10 mm, laser cut, hot-dip galvanised
Steel tube CHS 60.3 or 76.1 x 4 mm, round bar seat posts
Bolts M10 or M12 with 3d washers
